text:
Maya: Heads up — us-west-2 GPU pool showing ~22% capacity drop since 02:10 UTC. Noticed after the scheduled OOB firmware push.
Nate: Yep saw it. 3 racks (rack-17, rack-18, rack-19) got BMC v3.1.0. SecureBoot bit flipped on two racks; TPM attestation failing on the boot path so NVMe/GPU probes fail to register.
Srinivas: deploy-bot shows firmware job finished at 02:05 UTC: job/2026-03-18/usw2/fw-stage/9881 :thumbsup:
Maya: here's ipmitool from rack-18:
```
# ipmitool -I lanplus -H rack-18-bmc -U admin -P **** chassis bootparam get 5
Boot Flag: 0x03 (Force PXE, Force PXE)
Secure Boot: enabled
TPM Present: yes
``` 
Alice: oof. Secure Boot enabled is the mismatch — our image isn't signed for the new BMC policy. That would explain device probe failures.
Nate: Confirmed in systemd logs: `bmc-init: tpm: attestation failed - nonce mismatch` then `nvme-probe: no controller found` on affected hosts.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: firmware-stage job/9881 completed, /racks/{17,18,19} :information_source:
Srinivas: Immediate mitigation options:
• Rollback BMC to v3.0.8 on those 3 racks (fast but requires OOB reflash)
• Toggle SecureBoot policy off temporarily (risky for compliance)
• Drain and cold-provision in eu-west-1 for critical workloads
Maya: We can't toggle secure boot off in prod without OK from security. Suggest rollback + shift jobs to eu-west-1 as spillover.
Alice: Cost note — shifting ~120 GPU-hours/day to eu-west-1 will add roughly $9-13k/day until fixed (est). Also cold boots add extra latency for customer SLAs.
Nate: I'll start rollback run for rack-18 now. Runbook step:
```
1) SSH jump to oob-jumphost
2) `bmcflash --image v3.0.8.bin --target /dev/mgmt` 
3) monitor serial, watch for secureboot:false
4) uncordon after probe success
```
Maya: tagged INC-1234 and paged oncall. Will coordinate with security for exception window if rollback stalls.
Srinivas: If rollback fails, plan B is to advertise spare capacity and enable routing fallbacks; ops will prepare autoscale to compensate.
Maya: ok moving to action. I'll update thread with progress. :white_check_mark:
